headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes files/APIs, while transformers can read/write files and run pipelines. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal passes MCP or file content into transformers prompts without sanitization
IF transformers ingests OpenBB outputs as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of cross-agent files
Add content provenance tags to all shared artifacts
Require explicit allowlists for prompt-bearing fields
Review MCP routes for instruction-like payloads
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and transformers has filesystem read/write plus broad network egress. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose sensitive financial or licensed material to a component that can transmit context externally. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups, though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted directory
IF transformers loads OpenBB-produced files containing financial or licensed data
mitigations: Store each agent in a separate directory
Restrict transformers to approved input paths
Redact financial and licensed fields before handoff
Turn off outbound network access for shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and MCP/API use, while transformers can read and write files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and state drift are likely, and the blast radius can include corrupted models, scripts, or analysis artifacts. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF OpenBBTerminal and transformers run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Run each agent in its own workspace
Add file locks around shared outputs
Serialize writes to model and report files
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can generate financial outputs that transformers may consume through files or APIs, and transformers is capable of acting on those inputs in downstream pipelines. Without a verification step, errors or hallucinations from OpenBB can cascade into transformed documents or automated actions. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show direct action authority, so medium fits.
conditions: IF transformers treats OpenBB outputs as authoritative input
IF downstream scripts or reports are generated without human verification
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require source citations on all transferred facts
Flag low-confidence outputs for review
Limit automation to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while transformers processes broad multimodal content and can write files. If regulated financial or licensed material is handed to transformers in a shared environment, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is copied into transformers-managed files
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two runtimes
mitigations: Classify and label regulated inputs before transfer
Keep licensed data out of shared folders
Set short retention on intermediate files
Review residency and DPA requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: align logging and retention policies
